81802.subject: After the Click: Who Gets Paid in the New Internet Era 💸
81802.body:
View this post on the web at https://linas.substack.com/p/fintechpulse1146

Hey Everyone,
Good morning & happy Monday! Today, we’re diving deep into Alphabet’s and Reddit’s Q3 earnings, which wiped out more than $500B of market value in just 2 days, to see what they reveal about who makes money on the internet now that AI answers keep the clicks Google used to send to websites, and what founders, operators & investors should do about it (what actually broke in both earnings reports, why the traffic isn’t moving to ChatGPT, the new value chain of an answer-first internet, 5 rules for the economy after the click, playbooks for AI founders, traffic businesses & investors, & the 12-month watchlist that shows which future is winning + bonus deep dives into Why AI Agents Will Make Better Products Win [ https://substack.com/redirect/f55b1a18-2e28-41ec-8390-207536e4e183?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ] [according to Stripe CEO], a16z’s State of Markets 2026: The AI Playbook for Founders and Investors [ https://substack.com/redirect/03fb21c7-9c3b-4a27-8fb2-c9b63a0f5019?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ], & more inside). So let’s jump straight into the paradigm-defining stuff 🌶️
After the Click: Who Gets Paid in the New Internet Era 💸
Following the money 💸 On October 29, Alphabet $GOOGL  had the worst day in its history as a public company, losing roughly half a trillion dollars of market value in a single session. The next day Reddit $RDDT  had its own worst day, falling 29% in a quarter when its revenue grew 53%. Ouch! 🤕
The market read these as two unrelated stock stories, one about AI spending and one about a social platform’s traffic. That reading missed the point. Read together, they are the first clean numbers on how value is moving across the internet.
For 25 years the web ran on a simple deal:
Create useful content → Google sends traffic → websites make money.
That deal is now over. In its place, a toll economy is forming around three choke points: who owns user intent, who owns content that can’t be faked, and who completes the transaction. Each one is starting to charge, and everyone in between is starting to pay.
Picture a shopper choosing a pair of running shoes. She types the question into Google. A full answer comes back: three models, the trade-offs, the prices, a sponsored listing, and a “buy” button. She doesn’t open a single website. Then she does something no search model was built for. She opens Reddit directly and searches the same question, because she wants to know whether real runners agree with the machine.
Now look at who got what. The answer engine got the question and kept it. The community got the trust but not the referral. The publisher whose review trained the answer got nothing. The merchant got the sale, but only after paying for a sponsored slot inside an answer it didn’t write.
